instructions.content: NEVER use WebFetch for standard web pages when defuddle is available; raw HTML commonly contains 5-10x more tokens than the extracted content.
NEVER call defuddle parse without --md when readable content is the goal; without it defuddle returns raw HTML.
NEVER use -p when the user wants the page body; it returns one metadata property and silently discards the body text.
NEVER use > to save output; always use -o, because redirection can corrupt encoding on non-UTF-8 terminals.
Save output with -o file.md when persistence is needed.
Use defuddle parse <url> -p <field> (title, description, domain) when the user asks for metadata only.
Confirm the URL is a standard web page, not a SPA or an auth-required page, before running defuddle.
If the output is empty or only navigation text, fall back to WebFetch.
For a JavaScript-heavy SPA, use WebFetch or inform the user; defuddle cannot execute JavaScript.
For a login-gated or auth-required page, use WebFetch or inform the user; defuddle fetches without credentials.
For an API endpoint returning JSON, use a direct fetch or inform the user; defuddle is for HTML pages.
Use --json when both the HTML and the markdown are needed in one result.
If defuddle is not installed, install it with npm install -g defuddle.
When in doubt about a URL, try defuddle first rather than WebFetch.
